sessions.phase_label: Project definition and smart-contract prize mechanics
Backend, authentication, payment-provider, and site-content design
Mechanics simplification, ebook access, and production launch preparation
Production minting, payment, data, and reader debugging
Reward-accounting stabilization, reader fixes, and public launch

requirements.title: Project Branding
requirements.definition: The product is presented under the client-confirmed Project Rebuild name until a future client-approved rebrand.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the product name only; page copy, hero layout, and the possible future BooksOnChain platform are not merged into this Requirement.

requirements.title: Landing-Page Hero Content and Layout
requirements.definition: The landing-page hero communicates the ebook offer, price, referral rewards, and mint call to action in a readable responsive layout.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the above-the-fold copy, emphasis, CTA, and layout; book-cover sizing and FAQ content have independent change and failure trajectories.

requirements.title: FAQ, About, and Mission Content
requirements.definition: The site provides client-approved explanatory content for the product, referral mechanics, payments, prizes, ownership, and project mission.
requirements.boundary_note: Groups the tightly related informational pages and product copy, but excludes transactional modal copy and the landing-page hero because those are independently modified and verified.

requirements.title: Landing-Page Book Cover Display
requirements.definition: The ebook cover is displayed on the landing page at an aesthetically appropriate size without cropping, overlap, or loss of visibility.
requirements.boundary_note: Separated from general hero content because cover cropping and sizing repeatedly failed and changed independently of the surrounding copy.

requirements.title: Small Block Prize Mechanism
requirements.definition: The system funds and executes the independently evolving recurring Small Block prize draw using its configured trigger, winner count, and prize amount.
requirements.boundary_note: Winner count, prize amount, trigger, and pool size are attributes of one Small Block mechanism; ticket issuance, winner randomness, and claim UX remain independently testable Requirements.

requirements.title: Big Block Prize Mechanism
requirements.definition: The system funds and executes the separately configurable Big Block prize draw until the client removes that entire mechanism.
requirements.boundary_note: Kept separate from Small Block because it receives independent parameter changes and is later removed while Small Block remains active.

requirements.title: Prize Ticket Issuance and Reset
requirements.definition: Qualifying referral activity creates the applicable prize ticket counters, with tickets scoped to the current draw and reset or expired after that draw.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers ticket creation, counter separation, draw eligibility, and reset semantics; recipient selection for no-code mints and ticket display accuracy are separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Provably Fair Prize Winner Selection
requirements.definition: Prize winners are selected on-chain using Chainlink VRF with ticket-weighted random eligibility.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers randomness and winner selection only; prize thresholds, ticket accounting, and winner collection are independently changeable.

requirements.title: Prize Winner Collection Flow
requirements.definition: A prize winner can collect the awarded prize through the client-confirmed winner flow, including a conditional claim control when required.
requirements.boundary_note: Separated from winner selection because a draw may succeed while the claim or payout interaction fails or changes independently.

requirements.title: Aave Prize-Pool Yield Integration
requirements.definition: Prize-pool funds use Aave for yield generation while that integration remains required.
requirements.boundary_note: This is an independent protocol integration that can be removed without removing the underlying prize mechanism.

requirements.title: Referral Code Identity and Validation
requirements.definition: Each NFT's own mint number is its permanent referral code, and only already minted eligible NFTs can be accepted as referral codes.
requirements.boundary_note: Combines code identity and validity because both enforce the tokenId-based referral mechanism; payout routing and metadata rendering are separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Direct Referral Commission Payout
requirements.definition: When a valid referral code is used, the designated NFT holder receives the configured commission automatically.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers commission transfer for an explicitly supplied valid code; ticket issuance and no-code random routing can fail or change independently.

requirements.title: No-Referral Random Reward Allocation
requirements.definition: When no valid referral code is supplied, the commission and applicable prize ticket are assigned to a randomly selected existing NFT holder, subject to the confirmed first-mint exception.
requirements.boundary_note: Random recipient selection, finalization, commission, ticket pairing, and the one-off first-mint exception form one tightly coupled no-code allocation mechanism; presentation of the resulting totals is separate.

requirements.title: Primary Mint Revenue Allocation
requirements.definition: Each primary mint charges the configured price and divides proceeds among the founder, referral commission, and active prize pool according to the current allocation.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the economic split rather than payment-currency execution; USDC, ETH conversion, fiat processing, and tips have separate failure paths.

requirements.title: USDC Wallet Mint Flow
requirements.definition: A connected wallet can approve the required USDC and complete exactly one successful NFT mint, with no NFT or success state created from approval alone.
requirements.boundary_note: USDC approval-to-mint execution has its own repeated failure and fix trajectory, separate from ETH conversion and generic success-modal copy.

requirements.title: ETH Mint Conversion and Refund Flow
requirements.definition: A buyer can pay in ETH, obtain the exact USDC-denominated mint output through the configured swap route, and receive unused value back under the client-approved refund behavior.
requirements.boundary_note: Includes ETH quoting, swap execution, exact output, shortfall failure, and excess refund because they form one payment path; payment-option presentation is separate.

requirements.title: Mint Payment Method Selection and Disclosure
requirements.definition: The mint interface clearly shows which payment methods are available and lets the buyer choose among enabled wallet, ETH, USDC, and card paths without exposing unavailable options.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers selection and disclosure only; each payment rail owns its own execution lifecycle.

requirements.title: Transak Fiat Mint Integration
requirements.definition: The product supports card and supported wallet-based fiat purchasing through Transak, while allowing an explicitly crypto-only launch phase when the integration is deferred.
requirements.boundary_note: Provider selection, launch deferral, and eventual card minting are one independently evolving fiat-payment capability; wallet creation for fiat users is a distinct behavior.

requirements.title: Fiat Buyer Embedded Wallet and Reward Access
requirements.definition: A non-crypto fiat buyer receives an accessible non-custodial wallet experience that holds the NFT and rewards and can be reached through the buyer's email or dashboard flow.
requirements.boundary_note: Separated from Transak checkout because wallet provisioning and later reward access can evolve or fail independently of card processing.

requirements.title: Optional Mint Tipping
requirements.definition: The mint page lets a buyer select a preset or custom optional tip and sends that tip through a clearly explained separate transaction when required.
requirements.boundary_note: Tip amount selection, transfer, second-transaction disclosure, and self-tip handling are attributes of one tipping mechanism rather than separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Secondary-Sale Royalty Enforcement
requirements.definition: NFT secondary sales enforce the configured flat royalty through marketplace controls and direct the resulting funds according to the product's pool and founder rules without creating referral tickets.
requirements.boundary_note: ERC-721C or equivalent marketplace controls are implementation attributes of the royalty mechanism, not a separate Requirement.

requirements.title: Wallet Authentication
requirements.definition: Crypto users can authenticate through wallet-based Sign-In with Ethereum for minting, transfers, and protected wallet-owned resources.
requirements.boundary_note: Wallet authentication is independently enabled and used from email authentication and public unauthenticated access.

requirements.title: Email Magic-Link Authentication
requirements.definition: Users can access dashboard functions through low-friction email authentication such as magic links.
requirements.boundary_note: Authentication state is separate from general transactional email delivery because one can work while the other fails.

requirements.title: Public Unauthenticated Data Access
requirements.definition: Public data such as leaderboards and prize-pool values can be accessed without user authentication.
requirements.boundary_note: This is a distinct access mode rather than an attribute of wallet or email authentication.

requirements.title: Transactional Email Delivery
requirements.definition: The system sends required verification, mint, certificate, badge, referral, and prize notifications through the configured email provider.
requirements.boundary_note: Brevo provider configuration and the different notification types are attributes of one delivery service; login authorization remains under email authentication.

requirements.title: Mauritius Landing-Page Geoblock
requirements.definition: Access to the Project Rebuild landing page is blocked from Mauritius as requested by the client.
requirements.boundary_note: The geoblock is independent of the business jurisdiction's payment-provider eligibility and should not inherit fiat-provider scope.

requirements.title: NFT Badge Achievements
requirements.definition: NFTs receive the client-approved cosmetic achievement badges when their configured referral or participation milestones are reached.
requirements.boundary_note: Badge definitions, replacement, award thresholds, and award accuracy form one achievement mechanism; responsive row layout is independently changeable.

requirements.title: Responsive Badge Layout
requirements.definition: Badge displays use a balanced, readable responsive layout across desktop and mobile.
requirements.boundary_note: Separated from badge award logic because grid composition and mobile rendering can fail while the correct badges remain awarded.

requirements.title: Removable IPFS Ebook Storage
requirements.definition: The ebook PDF is stored through Pinata-backed IPFS in a manner that preserves the client's requested ability to stop pinning or take down the hosted copy.
requirements.boundary_note: Storage and takedown behavior are independent from ownership gating and reader navigation.

requirements.title: NFT-Holder-Only Ebook Access
requirements.definition: The ebook is encrypted and accessible only after the system verifies that the requesting wallet owns a valid project NFT.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers encryption, ownership verification, signing, and access denial; PDF page navigation and offline download are independently testable.

requirements.title: Ebook Reader Display and Navigation
requirements.definition: Authorized holders can open the ebook in the custom reader and navigate all pages using usable cursor, on-screen, keyboard, and supported mobile controls.
requirements.boundary_note: Reader rendering and navigation have their own failure trajectory after ownership decryption succeeds, so they are separate from access gating.

requirements.title: Optional Offline PDF Download
requirements.definition: Authorized holders are offered an optional PDF download for offline reading in addition to the default read-only viewer.
requirements.boundary_note: Downloading can be enabled, removed, or secured independently from the in-browser reader.

requirements.title: NFT Image and Asset Metadata Rendering
requirements.definition: Minted NFTs resolve and display their image, basic metadata, and ebook links correctly in supported product and wallet surfaces.
requirements.boundary_note: Image and asset-link resolution are distinct from numerical referral attributes and dashboard ownership indexing.

requirements.title: NFT Referral and Reward Metadata Accuracy
requirements.definition: Each NFT's metadata and detail attributes accurately show its own referral code, referrals, tickets, earnings, and badges from the authoritative state.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers NFT-level structured attributes; aggregate leaderboard accounting and image rendering have separate sources and failure trajectories.

requirements.title: NFT Resale State Transfer
requirements.definition: When an NFT is sold, the buyer receives the book, mint-number referral identity, earned badges, and any client-confirmed transferable active ticket state.
requirements.boundary_note: Ownership-state transfer is independent of royalty charging and primary mint behavior.

requirements.title: Dashboard NFT Ownership and Supply Accuracy
requirements.definition: The dashboard shows only successfully minted NFTs owned by the connected user and reports consistent token identifiers and total supply.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers ownership indexing, false mints, token numbering, and supply consistency; reward totals and NFT metadata are separate data products.

requirements.title: Referral Reward Accounting Accuracy
requirements.definition: Leaderboards and aggregate reward views accurately account for tickets, referrals, commissions, and earnings for both code-used and randomly assigned no-code rewards.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers aggregate accounting across reward surfaces; the underlying reward-routing rules and individual NFT metadata remain separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Prize Pool and Platform Statistics Accuracy
requirements.definition: Public and dashboard statistics accurately show mint totals, current prize-pool value, draw progress, and related platform counters.
requirements.boundary_note: Public pool and platform counters can fail independently from user-owned NFT indexing and referral reward totals.

requirements.title: Mint Success and Referral Feedback
requirements.definition: Mint success UI appears only after the real mint and any required reward finalization succeeds, displays the correct token ID, and uses outcome-specific referral or no-referral messaging.
requirements.boundary_note: Success gating, token ID, and referral-specific copy form one transaction-feedback mechanism; payment execution remains under the relevant payment-path Requirement.

requirements.title: Contract Upgrade Data Continuity
requirements.definition: Production contract upgrades preserve or deliberately migrate the intended active user, NFT, reward, and frontend state without silently mixing obsolete contracts.
requirements.boundary_note: This operational behavior is independently required because contract redeployments repeatedly caused data resets or cross-contract inconsistency.

requirements.title: Base Network Deployment
requirements.definition: The NFT product and its production smart-contract interactions operate on Base as the client-confirmed blockchain.
requirements.boundary_note: The target blockchain is a platform constraint, not a broad container for minting, royalties, or deployment debugging.

requirements.title: Discord Community Server
requirements.definition: The project provides a configured Discord community server with onboarding, announcements, discussion, feedback, support, bug-report, and product channels.
requirements.boundary_note: The server is an independently delivered operational artifact; it is not merged with the on-site support form.

requirements.title: On-Site Support Contact Form
requirements.definition: The site provides a help or contact form collecting the requested contact and inquiry fields, reachable through a clear support entry point.
requirements.boundary_note: The form is a standalone product behavior even if Discord and email provide additional support channels.

requirements.title: Wallet Safety Verification Submission
requirements.definition: The deployed project is submitted to the relevant wallet-security verification service to remove false malicious-site warnings.
requirements.boundary_note: This is a concrete production-verification task, not a general debugging or launch-management Requirement.

requirements.title: Production Contract Event Webhook
requirements.definition: Alchemy forwards all relevant Base Mainnet contract logs to the production backend so mint, referral, ticket, and related events can be indexed.
requirements.boundary_note: This is an independently required infrastructure behavior rather than generic setup activity because downstream reward and mint data depend on executable event ingestion.

requirements.title: Super Admin Control Panel
requirements.definition: A proposed administrative control panel would manage mints, referrals, prize pools, users, payments, and operational functions from one interface.
requirements.boundary_note: Kept visible because the client accepts the proposal, but the evidence may establish only a design document rather than implementation of the actual control panel.

requirements.title: Client Ownership of Mint Number One
requirements.definition: The client-designated wallet receives ownership of mint and affiliate code number one.
requirements.boundary_note: This is a one-off data-transfer obligation and not part of the general mint-number or referral-code rules.

unresolved_candidates.description: The desired non-custodial wallet experience for fiat buyers is clear, but the evidence does not establish whether Transak itself can create and expose that wallet exactly as described in the client-authored FAQ copy.
It is unclear whether the optional direct PDF download remains required after the later decision to encrypt and gate the ebook through Lit Protocol.
The accepted Super Admin item may require only a design document, not implementation of the control panel itself.
